title: A giver, Sīha, a donor, whatever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of nobles, brahmins, householders, or ascetics — he approaches with confidence, without…
content: A giver, Sīha, a donor, whatever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of nobles, brahmins, householders, or ascetics — he approaches with confidence, without hesitation or perplexity. This, Sīha, is a directly visible benefit of giving.

title: Elder Vāraṇa: Whoever among people harms other beings, That person harms himself in this life and the next. But one with a compassionate heart, pitying…
content:
Elder Vāraṇa:

Whoever among people harms other beings,
That person harms himself in this life and the next.

But one with a compassionate heart, pitying all beings,
A person acting thus reaps abundant merit.

Learn to speak well, serve the ascetics,
Live alone secluded, with a peaceful mind.

title: The thoughts of craving Are a person's sensual pleasures, The beautiful things in the world Are not the sensual pleasures, The thoughts of craving Are…
content:
The thoughts of craving
Are a person's sensual pleasures,
The beautiful things in the world
Are not the sensual pleasures,
The thoughts of craving
Are a person's sensual pleasures,
The beautiful things remain
As they are in the world,
But the wise
Subdue desire for them.

title: Elder Ukkhepakata Vaccha: Wealth accumulated over many months and years — The work of Vaccha, now Vaccha throws it away. Thus he teaches the laypeople,…
content:
Elder Ukkhepakata Vaccha:

Wealth accumulated over many months and years —
The work of Vaccha, now Vaccha throws it away.
Thus he teaches the laypeople,
Sitting properly in an honored seat, with vast joyful mind.

title: Possessing three qualities, bhikkhus, accordingly one is reborn in hell. What three? One kills living beings oneself, encourages others to kill, and approves of killing.…
content: Possessing three qualities, bhikkhus, accordingly one is reborn in hell. What three? One kills living beings oneself, encourages others to kill, and approves of killing. Possessing these three qualities, accordingly one is reborn in hell. Possessing three qualities, bhikkhus, accordingly one is reborn in heaven. What three? One abstains from killing oneself, encourages others to abstain from killing, and approves of abstaining from killing. Possessing these three qualities, accordingly one is reborn in heaven. One takes what is not given oneself ... One abstains from taking what is not given oneself ... One engages in sexual misconduct oneself ... One abstains from sexual misconduct oneself ... One speaks falsely oneself ... One abstains from false speech oneself ... One speaks harshly oneself ... One abstains from harsh speech oneself ... One is covetous oneself ... One is not covetous oneself ... One has ill-will oneself ... One does not have ill-will oneself ... One holds wrong view oneself ... One abstains from wrong view oneself ... Possessing these three qualities, accordingly one is reborn in heaven.

title: And, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple, who has seen the noble ones, is skilled in the teaching of the noble ones, trained in the teaching…
content: And, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple, who has seen the noble ones, is skilled in the teaching of the noble ones, trained in the teaching of the noble ones; who has seen the true persons, is skilled in the teaching of the true persons, trained in the teaching of the true persons — he regards form: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards feeling: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards perception: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards formations: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and reflected upon by the mind: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' And whatever views placeholders say: 'This is the world, this is my self; after death I will be permanent, everlasting, eternal, unchanging, and I will abide like that forever' — he regards that too: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' Thus regarding, he is not anxious or troubled about what does not actually exist.

title: Bhikkhus, regarding the view that is noble, leading upwards, leading to the complete destruction of suffering for one who practices accordingly — a bhikkhu lives…
content: Bhikkhus, regarding the view that is noble, leading upwards, leading to the complete destruction of suffering for one who practices accordingly — a bhikkhu lives possessing that view in common with his fellow celibates, both in private and in public. This principle of cordiality creates affection, creates respect, leading to cohesion, to non-dispute, to harmony, to unity.

title: Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, the bhikkhu enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination,…
content: Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, the bhikkhu enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and ease born of seclusion. He drenches, saturates, fills, and suffuses his body with the rapture and ease born of seclusion, so that no part of his entire body is not suffused with that rapture and ease born of seclusion.

title: The life of humans in this world is not known, Without sign, full of trouble, brief, bound to suffering. There is no effort by which…
content:
The life of humans in this world is not known,
Without sign, full of trouble, brief, bound to suffering.

There is no effort by which one can escape death.
After old age comes death — such is the nature of beings.

As ripe fruits are always in danger of falling,
So mortals, once born, are always in danger of death.

As a potter's clay vessels, large and small,
At last all break — so is the life of mortals.

title: And, friends, how is there fear of wrongdoing? Here, friends, a bhikkhu reflects: 'If evil, unwholesome states that have not arisen in me were to…
content: And, friends, how is there fear of wrongdoing? Here, friends, a bhikkhu reflects: 'If evil, unwholesome states that have not arisen in me were to arise, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. 'If evil, unwholesome states that have arisen in me are not abandoned, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. 'If wholesome states that have not arisen in me do not arise, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. 'If wholesome states that have arisen in me were to cease, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. Thus, friends, is there fear of wrongdoing. Thus, friends, having ardor and fear of wrongdoing, one is capable of enlightenment, capable of Nibbāna, capable of attaining the supreme security from bondage.
